summary: Samuel Slater was an Indology scholar educated at King's College London. He served as Rector at St. Paul's School, Darjeeling (1850), Professor at Bishop's College, Calcutta (1850–1863), Professor of Hindustani at King's College London (1861–1862), and headmaster of Bishop Cotton School (1863–1886).
Samuel Swinton Jacob was a history and archaeology specialist. He was educated at Cheam School and trained as an engineer at Addiscombe Military Seminary circa 1856–1858.
Samuel Tickell worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at Addiscombe Military Seminary from 1827 to 1829 and served in the Bengal Army circa 1829 to 1865.
Samuel Wells Williams was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute circa 1831–1832. He later held a post at Yale University from circa 1877 to 1884.

Samuel William Fallon worked in linguistics and Indology, earning a Ph.D. from Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg by 1862. He served as an inspector of schools for the Bengal Education Department circa 1857–1878.

Sandamali Udeshika Dissanayaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA from the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (2017–2021) and an MA from the University of Kelaniya (2023–2024). In 2024, she was a Temporary Lecturer at the University of Ruhuna.

Sandeep Namdev Dhikale works in Indology and religious studies and earned an M.A. from Savitribai Phule Pune University. He held positions at Fergusson College, the Ministry of Education, MIT World Peace University, and the Chhatrapati Shahu Maharaj Research, Training and Human Development Institute.
Sandford Arnot was an Indology and linguistics scholar. In 1826, he succeeded John Borthwick Gilchrist and served as a teacher of Hindustani at the Oriental Institution, Leicester Square.

Sandford Arthur Strong studied under Cecil Bendall, at King's College London, St John's College, and Oxford. Working in Indology and Buddhist studies, he was Lecturer of Assyriology at Cambridge (~1894–1903) and Professor of Arabic at University College London (1895).

Sandra A. Wawrytko is a scholar of philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. She taught Michael J. Tetreault and held appointments at San Diego State University, attested as Professor in 1999 and Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2014.
Sandra Bell is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She completed her doctoral thesis at Durham University by 1991 and served as a Professor there in 1991.
Sandra Hochwarter is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her Mag.phil. at the University of Vienna, where she studied under Anne MacDonald and MA supervisor Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Sang-Kyun Sun is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Delhi under supervisor Sanghasen Singh (attested 1995). In 1995, he was attested as a Lecturer at JinGak Buddhist College.

Sanga Tenzin earned a BSc from Navodaya Education Trust (2012–2016) and worked as a Clinical Nurse at Central Regional Referral Hospital in 2018. In Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he serves as Assistant Professor and HoD at CIHTS (attested 2026).

Sangay Dorji studied at Tengtho Monastery and Semtokha Rigney School, where he also taught. In Tibetology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, he was Secretary of the Dzongkha Development Commission (1999–2004) and Specialist at the Ministry of Education and Skills Development (2022).

Sangeeta Abhay Patil is an Indology scholar who earned an MD from Savitribai Phule Pune University (2005–2007). In 2023, she served as an Academic Consultant at Yashwantrao Chavan Maharashtra Open University.

Sangharakshita studied at Banaras Hindu University (~1949–1950) and under teachers including Jagdish Kashyap, Dhardo Rinpoche, Chien Ming Chen, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, and Dudjom Rinpoche. A Buddhist and religious studies figure, he founded the Triratna Buddhist Community in 1967.

Sangseraima Ujeed is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who completed a doctorate at the University of Oxford (~2013–2017). She held a Robert H. N. Ho postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Santa Barbara (~2018–2020).

Sangye Tenzin was an abbot at Menri Monastery in the fields of Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He taught Yongdzin Tenzin Namdak, Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche, Matthew T. Kapstein, and Michael J. Sweet, and was attested at UVA in 2026.

Sangyeob Cha is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at Dongguk University (2001–2008). He served as an HK Professor at Geumgang University (2011–2022) and as a Researcher at Kyungpook National University (2020).
